# Measured memory system - STM32F429ZI

*🤖WARNING🤖: This file LLM generated and may read oddly. Will eventually be human-edited for that real-life touch and typos.*

`memmap/1 STM32F429ZI cortex-m4 16000000 systick 16000000 icache,dcache,waitstates,ramfunc`

| property | measured | confidence |
|---|---|---|
| read width | 16 bytes | high |
| fill unit | unknown | none |
| latch | 1 entry x 16 B, depth 1; differential 5 cyc at waitstates=5 icache=0 dcache=0 prefetch=0; no knob reaches it | high |
| cache | 128 B, fully associative; 8 entries of 16 B fetched | high |
| replacement policy | LRU (measured against FIFO, not assumed) | high |
| waitstate scaling | 1 cycles per wait state | high |
| twin calibration | +0 cyc/access at 0 wait states in waitstates=0 icache=0 dcache=0 prefetch=0 (`walk` body)  (clean: the subtraction is unbiased) | high |

| knob | read width | latch | data reuse |
|---|---|---|---|
| `icache` | no effect | no effect | no effect |
| `dcache` | no effect | masks | controls |
| `prefetch` | no effect | no effect | no effect |

fill_unit caveats:
- Every knob setting saturates at the same stride, so no separate fill unit is distinguishable from the read width.

latch caveats:
- 2 configuration(s) are SILENT on this claim rather than evidence for or against it: waitstates=0 icache=0 dcache=0 prefetch=0, waitstates=0 icache=1 dcache=1 prefetch=1. In each the positive control fails - a hit and a miss differ by 0 cycles here (the same walk at `waitstates = 0`, where a flash access is known to cost no more than an SRAM one), below the 1-cycle resolution of an integer counter, so this configuration could not have shown a structure whether or not one is present - at LATENCY 0 in particular every flash structure reads flat by construction (MEASURING_CHANNELS B3) - so the flat column they produced is the resolution floor, not a register. A configuration that could not have shown the opposite does not get a vote.
- 14 knob setting(s) re-read fast at every offset. That is consistent with both the latch and a cache holding both probe addresses, so those settings do not discriminate; the latch is inferred there, not measured.

replacement_policy caveats:
- This uses the optional third argument to `evict`, which `flashmap/PROTOCOL.md` documents as an addendum. The host verifies the shim honours it by checking that the CHECKSUM changes, not the timing - a shim that silently ignored the argument would return the default walk and read as FIFO.

waitstate_scaling caveats:
- A wait-state setting of 0 contributes a legitimate zero to this fit and must not be read as an absent structure: at LATENCY = 0 a hit and a miss cost the same cycle, so the structure is still there and simply worth nothing (MEASURING_CHANNELS B3).
- At least one configuration shows a flat-zero differential at every wait state. That is the masking configuration (a cache holding both probe addresses), not evidence against the scaling.

Cross-checks:
- Cross-check: the latch granularity equals the flash read width (16 B), as it does on every part in this repository.
- SCOPE: every `evict` and `chase` row in this capture was taken at `waitstates = 5`, so the cache claim is a claim about that one setting. Nothing here suggests the geometry moves with the latency, and nothing here tests it either.
